design_feedback.direction: Combine inhabited frontages with sparse improvised pipes and channels.
design_feedback.right_edge: Fill the area beside the forge with subordinate connected structures.
design_feedback.market: Market needs a separate architectural redesign; retain its position.

variants.name: Connected neighborhood
variants.detail: VARIANT 06: Use staggered low inhabited service rooms on BOTH sides, with one small two-storey volume at the far left only. On the RIGHT, two compact attached rooms at right angles form an L-shaped frontage beside the forge, one sparse dim opaque window and a dark recessed plain maintenance door. A short supported awning and a thick pipe connect them to the forge's rear service area without crossing its entrance. The rightmost room crops naturally beyond frame; this town continues offscreen. Use a few slightly different roof planes and patched slate panels, but no towers. Left side is inhabited and irregular like image 2, less uniform than a long arcade. The result feels like an old town gradually fitted into huge infrastructure.
variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Make ONE polished concept paintover of a stylized game menu town called Respite.
Image 1 is the actual approved composition and EDIT TARGET. Images 2 and 4 are references for inhabited service frontages and sheltered walkways. Image 3 is a reference for sparse improvised pipes and recessed utility channels. Combine their useful design ideas into image 1.
LOCK image 1 camera, framing, perspective, the five main building positions/rotations/sizes/silhouettes, continuous habitat wall and giant background ribs. The complete horseshoe MARKET stays lower LEFT; the open STASH stays behind it; CODEX behind stash left of circular EXIT; observation TOWER immediately RIGHT of exit; one-drum FORGE to right of tower. Keep all five entrances visible. Keep the market unchanged for a later separate redesign. No cropping destinations, no extra gate. The tunnel goes through solid wall on BOTH sides; retain wall to BOTH frame edges.
The new direction is a livable maintained human neighborhood threaded with older patched machine utilities. Add moderately dense secondary architecture outside the court on BOTH LEFT AND RIGHT. The viewer must read a real enclosing town frontage, not five freestanding objects on an empty plane. Use a mix of simple habitable rooms, a few opaque windows, practical covered passages, old short pipe runs and flush ground channels, all physically connected with believable supports/endpoints. Sparse broad patch panels suggest repair. Low-frequency soft matte scuffs and simple beveled game geometry; retain navy/cobalt/violet atmosphere and cyan exit emphasis. Restrained warm light, mostly shaded secondary structures. Avoid rows of equally bright lamps or equally bright doors that compete with gameplay entrances. At most one small subdued plant cluster, no decorative planter borders.
CRITICAL RIGHT EDGE: The empty space BESIDE AND IN FRONT-RIGHT OF THE FORGE needs architectural enclosure. Add a low secondary frontage that starts at the rear wall immediately RIGHT of the forge, turns forward along the far RIGHT edge of the court, and continues out of the RIGHT image crop. A real 3D volume must occupy the rightmost strip around the forge's side, not just a thin pipe against the far wall. Keep it lower and darker than the forge so the forge stays the dominant destination. Its front portion may extend down the right frame edge to about three-quarters of image height, with the low roof visible. Retain a broad clear central/foreground plaza and a usable open area INSIDE this edge for later expansion; do not preserve a completely bare right edge. No huge foreground wall or object blocks camera.
On LEFT, combine modest connected habitable volumes behind market/stash with a partial supported walkway leading toward Codex and rear wall. Narrow paths between existing destinations remain open.
Use two restrained purposeful pipe runs and recessed segmented service channels to tie town frontages and destination bases together. Some irregular offsets and repaired metal joints, not perfectly uniform new construction. Ground uses broad quiet paving patches and subtle perimeter changes, not dense regular tiny tiles or exaggerated mottling. No people, robots, vehicles, microscopic goods, dense machinery clutter, trees, statues, fountain, cliff, rail over abyss, wet mirrors, toy colours or repetitive neon frames.
No labels, no UI, no text. About 2:1 landscape, one image.
VARIANT 06: Use staggered low inhabited service rooms on BOTH sides, with one small two-storey volume at the far left only. On the RIGHT, two compact attached rooms at right angles form an L-shaped frontage beside the forge, one sparse dim opaque window and a dark recessed plain maintenance door. A short supported awning and a thick pipe connect them to the forge's rear service area without crossing its entrance. The rightmost room crops naturally beyond frame; this town continues offscreen. Use a few slightly different roof planes and patched slate panels, but no towers. Left side is inhabited and irregular like image 2, less uniform than a long arcade. The result feels like an old town gradually fitted into huge infrastructure.

variants.name: Covered service court
variants.detail: VARIANT 07: Build a coherent low covered passage behind the LEFT buildings like image 4, interrupted by one squat enclosed service room and a narrow side-lane opening. For the RIGHT side, form a small forge service yard with a solid back room against the wall, a low roofed maintenance bay extending FORWARD along the right edge, and one chunky closed equipment housing under the roof. The bay has three plausible square supports, no detailed workshop tools or visible merchandise. Its roof height stays below the forge drum; its right edge crops out of frame. Thick short connected pipes, one valve housing and a recessed utility channel physically unite the right bay to the forge and wall. The yard is a legible shared support area and makes a firm right boundary to the plaza, with the central approach fully open. Mostly closed simple volumes, economical modelling, no busy industrial factory infestation.
